steps.name: Normalize counts and flag low-library sample
caveats: Do not drop sample_01 silently — report its library size and flag it in QC output so downstream score interpretation can account for it; only exclude it if normalization diagnostics show it is unusable
steps.question: How should the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 13 columns, 12 UC-inflamed/control samples plus metadata) be normalized to produce a matrix suitable for single-sample pathway scoring, given sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix is loaded from counts.csv (genes x samples) and metadata.csv (condition per sample) and merged/aligned by sample ID
Library sizes are computed and reported for all samples, explicitly flagging sample_01 as an outlier (~4x below median)
Counts are normalized for library size and composition (e.g., edgeR TMM or DESeq2 median-of-ratios) and log-transformed (e.g., log2(CPM+1) or vst) to produce a normalized expression matrix
Output is a gene x sample normalized expression matrix (CSV or RDS) plus a QC note on sample_01 retained for downstream steps

steps.name: Compute per-sample hallmark pathway activity scores (GSVA) and heatmap
caveats: GSVA needs a reasonable minimum sample size per group for stable kernel estimation; with n=6 per group note this in output as a limitation on score stability
Confirm gene symbol capitalization/format matches between counts.csv and the hallmark GMT before running GSVA — mismatches silently drop genes from sets
steps.question: What is the per-sample activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways across the 12 ulcerative-colitis-inflamed vs control colon samples, and which pathways visually separate the two groups in a heatmap?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the normalized gene x sample expression matrix from T1S1 as input, with gene symbols matching HGNC identifiers

Loads the MSigDB human Hallmark gene set collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols) staged in this environment; if absent, reports the gap and stops rather than substituting a non-human or non-hallmark collection
Runs GSVA (or ssGSEA method within the GSVA package) to produce a sample x pathway (12 samples x 50 hallmark pathways) activity score matrix, saved as a CSV

Produces a heatmap of the score matrix (samples as columns, hallmark pathways as rows) with a top annotation bar for condition (UC-inflamed vs control), using pheatmap or ComplexHeatmap, with rows clustered so pathways separating the two groups are visually grouped
Heatmap and score matrix are saved as output files

steps.name: Rank hallmark pathways separating UC-inflamed from control
caveats: Do not overclaim mechanistic pathway engagement — GSVA/hallmark scores indicate coordinated expression shift, not confirmed pathway activity
With only 12 samples total, correct for multiple testing across 50 pathways (BH) and report this explicitly rather than using raw p-values
steps.question: Which of the 50 hallmark pathway activity scores differ significantly (moderated t-test, BH-adjusted) between the 6 UC-inflamed and 6 control colon samples?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the sample x pathway GSVA score matrix from T2S1 as input, joined to the condition labels from metadata.csv
Runs a moderated t-test (limma) or equivalent per-pathway two-group comparison (UC-inflamed vs control, unpaired, n=6 vs n=6) on the 50 hallmark scores
Reports effect size (mean score difference), t/p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per pathway, sorted by adjusted p-value

Output table explicitly separates statistically significant pathways (adjusted p < 0.05) from those only visually distinct in the heatmap, and states that n=6/6 limits power to detect anything but moderate-to-large effects
sample_01's flagged low library size is checked as a potential leverage point on any top-ranked pathway (e.g., report if removing it changes significance)

plan.title: Hallmark pathway activity scoring, UC vs control colon
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 samples — 12 used, one extra) with 6 ulcerative-colitis-inflamed vs 6 control colon samples, unpaired, single batch. sample_01 has a ~4x-below-median library size, which will distort variance-stabilized expression and any downstream per-sample pathway score if left uncorrected, so normalization is handled explicitly before scoring. The research question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score (not a group-level DE contrast) plus a heatmap showing which hallmark pathways separate treated from control. This is answered directly with single-sample gene set enrichment (ssGSEA/GSVA) against the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols) staged in this environment, which matches the organism (Homo sapiens) and gene identifier space (gene symbols, per the counts file). Step 1 normalizes counts on the bulk-transcriptomics agent (library-size normalization, log-transform, QC flag on sample_01). Step 2 computes GSVA per-sample hallmark scores on the normalized matrix and produces the sample x pathway score matrix plus a heatmap annotated by condition, run on the enrichment agent since the primary object at that point is a generic score matrix, not raw counts. Step 3 statistically ranks which hallmark pathways differ between UC-inflamed and control using the per-sample scores (moderated t-test / limma), closing the loop on 'which pathways separate treated from control' with a p-value rather than visual impression alone.
